title: Scale-signal derate window bias causing reserved pool headroom drain during regional failover
creator: Asha Kothari
description:
Summary: During an inter-region failover exercise on 2025-10-03 we observed several Dedicated reserved pools rapidly lose apparent headroom and subsequently serve elevated 429/504s for a subset of tenants. The autoscaler did not allocate expected burst capacity until tens of seconds later, which caused customer-visible errors for mid- and high-SLA tenants. This ticket tracks the root cause investigation, the emergency mitigation that shipped, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.

Why this matters: A miscalculation in the scale signal derate logic caused the autoscaler to conservatively withhold capacity during a period where we needed aggressive re-warm/scale-up behavior. Multiple enterprise customers experienced degraded throughput at peak traffic windows and filed escalations.

Scope: Impacted Dedicated pools in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 during roll traffic and failover testing; both hosted and Dedicated customers saw increased tail latency when routed to affected pools. Private (VPC) deployments were unaffected.

Observed signals: persistent allocation deficit in allocator metrics, queue growth in per-tenant inflight queues, KV-cache cold-starts, and burst-credit counters dropping to zero even when capacity existed in the cloud provider. Autoscaler logs showed repeated derate events that never reconciled.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure a reserved pool with conservative warmup policy and per-tenant burst caps.
2) Simulate regional weight shift (failover) by moving 40% of traffic from us-east-1 to us-west-2.
3) Trigger a scale-down + immediate scale-up cycle by toggling test traffic envelope.
4) Observe allocator_headroom metric and per-tenant queue length; assert that headroom remains artificially low for >20s and requests are queued/429ed.
5) Reproduce requires coordinator retry path (leader change) under high cardinality tenants to surface the aggregation bug.
root_cause: A regression in scale_signal_aggregator introduced a biased derate window calculation: (a) the derate window used wall-clock timestamps instead of monotonic clocks resulting in time-skew when the leader migrated between processes; (b) the aggregator applied a cumulative min() over derate contributions across tenants when it should have been a per-sample, per-tenant exponential decay. The combination caused derate to persist across leader restarts and to compound when coordinator retries occurred, producing an overly conservative scale signal that undervalued headroom and suppressed immediate scale-up. This is algorithmic (signal math + clock source) rather than a provisioning or quota leak.
mitigation_and_rollout:
Emergency mitigation applied 2025-10-04: 1) Feature-flagged a temporary bypass that ignores derate contributions for 10s after leader election; 2) Relaxed safety-window threshold in control-plane config from 120s -> 30s for affected regions; 3) Deployed hotfix to autoscaler (PR rwi/autoscaler#3478) that corrects clock source to monotonic and replaces cumulative-min with per-sample exponential decay.
Rollout plan: Canary in us-west-2 with 3 pools (2025-10-05 03:00 UTC) -> progressive ramp to 25% of dedicated capacity -> full global rollout 2025-10-06. We tagged the build runtime-1.32.0-hotfix and added a rollout monitor dashboard.
Emergency customer remediation: For top-tier customers affected we executed a temporary route override to fallback models/regions and manually bumped reserved capacity for two hours while canary completed.
follow_up_tasks: Add deterministic unit tests for derate window math and leader-change behavior
Instrument monotonic-clock usage across all aggregator components
Add high-cardinality tenant scenarios to chaos tests (leader churn + burst traffic)
Create autoscaler observability alert: prolonged_derate_persistence (>10s) -> incident page
Convene design review for derate semantics and safety-window tradeoffs
Postmortem and customer-facing incident summary draft
